known_limitations: This shard was produced by a single packet-only worker without compiler/toolchain access; token counts and fact-state classifications were derived analytically against the Go language specification and standard library documentation rather than mechanically re-verified with an automated tokenizer/build, per the packet-only constraint (no local filesystem/shell/process tools).

The 0-100 normalized figure reported here (raw_density*100) is Go's own figure computed on Go's all-fragments basis (44/44). Per interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule, the authoritative comparison figure requires the runner to recompute density on the common basis (probes where ALL 10 languages have a fragment) once every language shard is merged; this worker cannot compute that basis alone.
metric.semantic_density.methodology_note: Raw value per spec 6.1.3.A = (explicit-local semantic sites)/(lexical source tokens), counted over the measured_fragment of each of the 44 frozen probes. This shard covers Go only; the normalized score reported is raw_density*100 (density values are inherently <1 because most probes require several tokens per semantic fact). Cross-language common-basis reconciliation (probes where ALL 10 languages have a fragment) must be performed by the runner once all language shards are merged; this shard reports the Go all-fragments figure (basis size = 44, n_L = 44 since a fragment or a named/PARTIAL substitute was authored for every probe) and flags it as such.

metric.semantic_density.tokenizer_rule: Language-neutral lexer-style tokenizer: each keyword, identifier, operator, and individual punctuation mark (including each bracket/comma/colon/semicolon) is one token; numeric and string literals count as a single token each; comments and whitespace are excluded; cgo pragma-comment lines (e.g. //export) are excluded from the token count as comments even though they carry compiler semantics for Go, per the frozen comment-exclusion rule.
